items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: I tell you what, back then I was influenced by Roy Brown, T-Bone Walker, and mostly Roy Brown

ctx.x: Yeah, I wrote Shrewsbury Blues and I wrote the flip side, I think it was Early Dawn Boogie. And I tell you what, back then I was influenced by Roy Brown, T-Bone Walker, and mostly Roy Brown, because Roy Brown was very, very popular at that time. And I remember, see this is the beginning, this is right in the early stages of my singing career. I was singing on Shrewsbury Road by Sam Gennaro's place, and Bama had a Dixieland band there. And I used to go in there and sing, you know, and we would get a quarter,…
and stuff for singing a specific song.

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: He came down here with Roy Brown.

ctx.x: Who's your favorite drummer? Who could play? Right now, today? No, not today. What's the thing about, William?

You know, uh, there was nobody better than Earl Palmer, man, for recording, for whatever. You know, I remember Earl, Earl one time, we was in the Dew Drop, and this drummer came down here. He OD'd. He came down here with Roy Brown. Heck of a drummer. I can't remember his name. But boy, he could play. But boy, he could play. And so, one night, we was all in the Dew Drop listening to him. And, uh, when he finished, I told Earl, I said, why don't you go ahead and sit in, man? He said, man, the captain played…
